messages:
Devon: Quick follow-up from the GQA/MQA RFC — we need to finalize runtime behavior before the canary. Three open items: 1) kernel selection heuristic, 2) KV-cache layout + memory accounting, 3) model compatibility / upgrade path. Share short takes?

Maya: +1. My leaning is runtime-decide at request-time. Heuristic inputs: seq_len, batch_size, head_dim, is_streaming, quant_mode.

Samir: Microbench highlights to consider (local rig, A100 40GB):
Samir: - head_dim=64, batch=1..4, seq<=512: MQA uses ~30% less GPU mem, latency 5-12% slower than GQA.
Samir: - head_dim=128, seq>=1024: GQA throughput ~1.3x higher; kernel fusion benefits show up for long contexts.
Samir: - streaming requests (small incremental tokens) favor MQA due to smaller KV-touch per token.

Olga: Important quant caveat: per-channel 8-bit quant produced higher accumulation noise for MQA paths in our tests. Observed output token distribution drift ~=0.6% KL vs FP16 baseline on eval prompts. We should auto-block MQA for any model/quant combo where quality_regression_pct > 0.5.

Lee: UX/SDK note: if runtime auto-switches silently, operators will get confused when outputs shift. Propose model manifest include an `attention_modes` field and a `preferred_mode` fallback. Also expose an API query param `attention_mode=auto|gqa|mqa` for debuggability.

Nora: telemetry idea: log decision reasons per request (anonymized): {mode, seq_len, batch, head_dim, quant_mode, reason_tag}. That'll let us refine heuristics without user-visible churn.

Devon: Good. For KV-cache layout: we need a deterministic on-disk and in-memory mapping so canaries and clients can reuse cached prefixes across mode switches where possible. Two options:
Devon: 1) Unified KV layout: store per-layer keys as [mode-agnostic] tensors and add a lightweight mapping layer at runtime to reinterpret for GQA vs MQA (more CPU work on switch).
Devon: 2) Separate caches: maintain distinct caches per mode (higher mem, simpler kernels).

Samir: Perf tradeoff: unified cache reduces duplication but needs remapping that costs ~0.3ms/token in our bench. Separate caches cost extra memory (up to 1.4x) but zero remap overhead.

Olga: For private deployments with tight memory (Dedicated small configs), separate cache will OOM. We need a policy: prefer unified cache if GPU_memory_free < threshold.

Lee: Manifest snippet proposal (for converters / offline tooling):
Lee: ```json
Lee: {
Lee:   "model_name": "redwood-open-x",")
Lee:   "attention_modes": ["gqa","mqa"],
Lee:   "preferred_mode": "gqa",
Lee:   "quant_compat": {"8bit_per_channel": false, "8bit_per_tensor": true}
Lee: }
Lee: ```
Lee: (note: will include schema in the model registry docs)

Nora: Also recommend adding a `mode_compat_issues` table in the registry where converter can record warnings like "mqa: quant-error > 0.5%". UI shows warnings during deploy/canary.

Devon: Canary plan: 1) Default runtime=auto in canary pool. 2) Enable per-request telemetry and quality regression checks (eval prompts). 3) Start 5% traffic, watch cost/latency/quality deltas for 48h. 4) If quant-related regressions occur, auto-pin to preferred_mode and surface a warning.

InfraBot: Canary cluster `gqa-mqa-switch-canary` created (id: canary-202611). Autoscaler off, observability hooks attached.

Maya: One more heuristic suggestion: add a tiny ML model (decision tree or small MLP) trained on microbench logs to predict best mode per (seq,batch,head,quant). It can be updated continuously from telemetry.

Samir: +1. We can ship a simple rule-based fallback first (thresholds: seq>=1536 => GQA, head_dim<=64 && seq<=512 => MQA, streaming => MQA), then replace with learned policy after two weeks of canary data.

Olga: Action items from me: run quant stress tests for all converter-supported quant types and produce `mode_compat_issues` CSV.

Lee: Action: PR for model manifest schema and SDK param; add `attention_mode` to inference call proto.

Devon: I'll own the runtime heuristic PR and canary orchestration. Let's aim to freeze behavior next Tue.

Nora: I'll wire telemetry + dashboards and a regression alert that flips canary to safe_mode on >0.5% eval drift.

Devon: Perfect. If nobody objects, we'll proceed with the canary plan. :thumbsup:
